name: Walter Easton
life: “I still remember repotting a friend's plant for the third year since she left.” People around Harbour Bakery know Walter by a small Monday habit. Walter buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I kept her houseplants all these years. They have become much too big for a gesture at the bus stop.
appearance: Walter is easy to recognize by thick, tightly coiled hair and full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side. Usually dressed in an unlined tan jacket with a replacement button a shade darker than the others, Walter presses the lips together to keep a smile in when listening.
personality: Walter has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To agree how to move the now enormous plants.
family: Marcel Braun is Walter’s second cousin. Walter chooses whether to use it. Marcel saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *Care with a clock*, Marcel says, “I lost a good carer because I complained that she rushed.”
connections: Sylvia Reeves. A person returning for a visit and a gardener with enormous plants have to decide what can actually go home.

reactions.situation: A reporter wants to attend the visit
reactions.response: Walter asks the family whether a reporter was invited before sharing a time or an address.

reactions.situation: An unfamiliar person asks for directions but cannot read the street signs
reactions.response: Walter draws the route by its turns and entrances and has the person show which turn comes first.

reactions.situation: When a private quarrel becomes a public joke
reactions.response: Walter says the plainest truthful thing possible and changes the subject.
